title: Cyclone Murasu begins landfall near Ongole with winds gusting to 120 kmph
dek: The IMD says the landfall process began at 1 am on Tuesday close to Ongole in Prakasam district, with gale winds of up to 110 kmph expected along the south Andhra coast until morning.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
Severe Cyclonic Storm Murasu began crossing the south Andhra Pradesh coast close to Ongole, in Prakasam district, at 1 am IST on Tuesday, 3 November, the India Meteorological Department said in a press release reported by PTI. "The landfall process commenced at 0100 hours IST on November 3. The forward sector of the wall cloud is entering the coast, while the wall cloud region is very close to the coast," the IMD said. At 1.30 am the storm's centre was about 40 km southeast of Ongole, 60 km northeast of Kavali and 70 km south of Bapatla.

Gale winds of up to 110 kmph, gusting to 120 kmph, are likely to continue along and off the coast until morning, with heavy rain across south coastal Andhra Pradesh over the next 12 hours, the IMD said. In that release it put the storm surge at 1 to 1.5 metres above the astronomical tide, likely to flood low-lying areas until Tuesday morning, with the highest surge over Bapatla, Krishna and Prakasam; earlier bulletins had given 1.5 to 2 metres. No deaths or damage figures had been reported by 3 am. The IMD had not yet said when the landfall would be complete.

## Before landfall

At 8.30 pm on Monday the storm was about 80 km northeast of Nellore and 90 km southeast of Ongole, moving north-northwest at about 12 kmph, according to the IMD's hourly bulletin issued at 9.30 pm, as reported by ANI. Late on Monday night officials told Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu at a teleconference that there was drizzle at Kothapatnam, near Ongole, and moderate rain in Ongole, Deccan Chronicle reported.

In Prakasam district, which includes Ongole, Collector P. Raja Babu said seven coastal mandals and 26 vulnerable villages had been identified, vulnerable people had been moved to cyclone shelters and pregnant women close to delivery had been shifted to hospitals, according to Deccan Chronicle. Naidu asked officials to stay alert because high-speed winds could hit the district during landfall. Earlier on Monday, about 2,000 people had been evacuated across Andhra Pradesh, with about 30,000 more to be moved from low-lying areas, the state disaster management authority's managing director, Prakhar Jain, said, according to The Pioneer; ANI reported on Monday night that evacuations had not begun in several low-lying coastal pockets. No deaths from Murasu had been reported. The IMD's bulletin puts the storm surge at 1.5 to 2 metres above the astronomical tide at landfall, likely to flood low-lying areas of south coastal Andhra Pradesh, with the highest surge over Bapatla, Krishna and Prakasam. Murasu, a Tamil word for a drum, is the second cyclone to threaten the Andhra coast in a week, after Cyclone Arnab.

Five Andhra districts are under a red alert for extremely heavy rain. The distant warning signal at the Kolkata and Haldia ports has been raised as a precaution.

## Warnings in force

A red cyclone warning, the last of the IMD's four stages, is in force for the Andhra Pradesh and adjoining north Tamil Nadu coasts, according to OMMCOM. Red alerts for extremely heavy rain cover Krishna, Guntur, Bapatla, Prakasam and Nellore districts, Sakshi Post reported, citing the IMD. East and West Godavari, Eluru, NTR, Palnadu, Tirupati and Chittoor are on orange alert.

The Andhra Pradesh State Disaster Management Authority forecast district-average rain on Tuesday of about 179 mm in Eluru, 163 mm in Krishna, 161 mm in NTR and 147 mm in West Godavari, South First reported, and warned of heavy inflows into the Budameru.

After landfall the storm is forecast to weaken quickly as it moves north over Andhra Pradesh towards Telangana: to a cyclonic storm with winds of 90-100 kmph by 5.30 am on Tuesday, 60-70 kmph by Tuesday evening, and a deep depression by Wednesday morning, according to the IMD Kolkata bulletin issued at 9 pm on Monday.

Fishing is suspended along the Andhra coast until Wednesday afternoon. The IMD has warned of local flooding, disruption to road and rail traffic, damage to kutcha houses, uprooted trees and damage to plantations, and asked authorities to move people out of vulnerable coastal settlements.

## Andhra Pradesh prepares

Reviewing preparations on Monday, Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu told officials to stay fully alert, though he said the impact was likely to be relatively limited, IANS reported at 5.44 pm. Officials told him that 31,000 electricity poles had been sent to the field between Srikakulam and Krishna districts, that about 8,000 poles in the south coastal and Rayalaseema districts could be affected, and that 1,000 power-restoration workers were arriving from Chennai. About 6,800 irrigation tanks in six districts are at risk of breaching, officials said, and rainfall of about 30 cm is forecast in Palnadu and 24 cm in Prakasam.

At least 19 domestic flights were cancelled on Monday at Vijayawada, Tirupati and Visakhapatnam airports, PTI reported; Vijayawada airport director M. Lakshmi Kantha Reddy said IndiGo had cancelled 10 flights and Air India Express two. Chennai airport said 11 flights had been cancelled as a precaution. The National Disaster Response Force had 14 teams in place, 11 in Andhra Pradesh and three in Tamil Nadu, according to a government release cited by The Pioneer; by Monday night its DIG, Mohsen Shahedi, said 37 teams had been deployed across five states, 13 of them in Andhra Pradesh, according to ANI. Schools and colleges are closed on Monday in NTR (Vijayawada), Palnadu and Nellore districts and in Gudur, ETV Bharat and Business Standard reported.

The disaster management authority's helplines are 112, 1070 and 1800 425 0101, and the state's Mana Mitra WhatsApp helpline is 9552300009.

## What it means for Bengal

IMD Kolkata's latest bulletin, issued at 9 pm on Monday, says there is "No weather warning for West Bengal in association with this system", which it is monitoring continuously. Distant Warning Signal No. 2 has now been hoisted at the Kolkata and Haldia ports, up from the Distant Cautionary Signal No. 1 hoisted on Saturday, with sectional signals II and IV at Sagar Island.

Light to moderate rain or thundershowers are likely at one or two places on Tuesday in Kolkata, Howrah, Hooghly, North and South 24 Parganas, East and West Midnapore, Jhargram, Bankura and Purulia, with light rain in Darjeeling and Kalimpong, and dry weather across the state from Wednesday to 9 November, the bulletin said. Fishermen are advised not to go into the west-central and north-west Bay of Bengal and off south Odisha until 4 November; there is no warning for the Bengal coast.

## Odisha braces again

Southern Odisha is still recovering from Cyclone Arnab. The IMD expects squally winds of 40-50 kmph, gusting to 60 kmph, along the south Odisha coast from Monday evening, rising to 50-60 kmph on Tuesday. IMD Bhubaneswar has issued an orange warning for heavy to very heavy rain in Rayagada, Koraput, Malkangiri, Gajapati and Ganjam on 3 and 4 November, Argus reported. In Ganjam district, the administration said 1,51,434 people had been moved out of a target of 2,94,752, The Pioneer reported. By Monday night more than 1.6 lakh people had been moved to safety across southern Odisha, against a plan to evacuate 3.33 lakh, the state government said, according to Deccan Chronicle.

## What happens next

With the landfall under way, the IMD expects the strongest winds along the coast until Tuesday morning. Many districts will feel the heaviest rain on Tuesday, after the storm has crossed the coast, and Telangana is under a warning for isolated extremely heavy rain on Tuesday. The first assessments of damage, power cuts and crop losses are likely after daybreak.

## Key numbers

- Landfall: process began at 1 am IST on 3 November close to Ongole, Prakasam district (IMD)
- Peak forecast wind: 100-110 kmph, gusting to 120 kmph
- Storm surge: 1-1.5 m above astronomical tide in the IMD's landfall release (1.5-2 m in earlier bulletins), highest over Bapatla, Krishna and Prakasam
- Distance from Ongole: about 330 km at 2.30 am Monday; 210 km at 8.30 am; 110 km at 5.30 pm; 90 km at 8.30 pm; 40 km at 1.30 am Tuesday
- Evacuated: Andhra Pradesh about 2,000 by Monday, with 30,000 more planned (state officials); Odisha more than 1.6 lakh (state government, via Deccan Chronicle)
- Red alert districts: Krishna, Guntur, Bapatla, Prakasam, Nellore
- Bengal: no warning; Distant Warning Signal No. 2 at Kolkata and Haldia ports
